primary_track: Track 02 — The Agent That Can Explain Why
query: Why did Q3 enterprise retention drop across our Computer & Office Equipment accounts, and how do SEC EDGAR revenues compare with our internal support escalation and billing tables?
executive_summary: Investigation for query "Why did Q3 enterprise retention drop across our Computer & Office Equipment accounts, and how do SEC EDGAR rev": Q3 enterprise net retention in Computer & Office Equipment (Industry Group 357) dropped to 86.99% ($-2,469,500 ARR delta across 7 enterprise accounts / 310 billing events), contrasting sharply with 103.0% net retention in Prepackaged Software (SIC 7372). Two compounding root causes explain both the operational decline and the reporting discrepancy: (1) Operational Driver: a 6.77x surge in P1 escalations (13 -> 88) caused by `v4.2_batch_connector_gateway_timeout` (peak p99 latency 2140ms, Pearson r = 0.96 with retention loss, $530,000 SLA credits issued), compounded by $2,085,000 in Q4 regional weather SLA risk; and (2) Taxonomic Data Blindspot: IBM (CIK 0000051143, $62.753B FY2025 revenue, -$730K Q3 ARR) self-reports SEC SIC code `3570` (a 3-digit Industry Group summary header absent from the 4-digit US SIC V4 leaf table `company_dns.sic_codes`), causing naive inner joins to silently drop IBM until caught by Zetaris DQ rule `fk_sic_check`. Unverified Hypothesis H4 (pricing-tier changes) was blocked by EvidenceEvaluatorAgent due to zero supporting rows.

why_explanation.primary_operational_driver: v4.2 batch connector gateway timeouts and storage telemetry stream backpressure caused a 6.77x surge in P1 escalations (13 -> 88 tickets) and p99 latency spikes up to 2,140ms (r = 0.96 with Q3 retention drop).
why_explanation.primary_data_discrepancy_driver: SEC EDGAR self-reported SIC code 3570 for IBM (CIK 0000051143) is a 3-digit Industry Group summary header, not a 4-digit leaf code in `company_dns.sic_codes` (3571..3577), causing naive joins to silently drop $62.753B in FY2025 enterprise revenue and $4.12M in Q3 ARR.
why_explanation.q4_forward_risk_driver: $2,085,000 in Q4 regional weather SLA penalty exposure across Industry Group 357 datacenters (led by IBM $620K in us-east-ny and Cisco $390K in us-east-nc), plus $490K for Dominion Energy (SIC 4911).
why_explanation.epistemological_boundary: Hypothesis H4 (Enterprise Pricing-Tier Changes) was blocked by EvidenceEvaluatorAgent and moved to untested_factors because zero pricing-tier change rows exist in Zetaris.

verified_findings.title: v4.2 Batch Connector Gateway Timeouts & P1 Ticket Surge (Primary Operational Driver)
verified_findings.explanation: Across the 7 Computer & Office Equipment accounts (SIC 3570/3571/3572/3575/3577), Q3 P1 support escalations jumped 6.77x (from 13 to 88 tickets) driven by `v4.2_batch_connector_gateway_timeout` and `storage_telemetry_stream_backpressure`. API p99 latency peaked at 2140ms (Pearson r = 0.96 with retention contraction), triggering $530,000 in Q3 SLA credit payouts and reducing cohort net retention to 86.99% ($-2,469,500 ARR delta).

verified_findings.title: SEC EDGAR SIC 3570 vs. US SIC V4 4-Digit Leaf Orphan ($62.753B Revenue Blindspot)
verified_findings.explanation: Zetaris Data Quality rule `fk_sic_check` proved why BI dashboards understated Computer & Office Equipment exposure: IBM (CIK 0000051143) files under SEC SIC code `3570` (a 3-digit Industry Group summary header), which does not exist in the 4-digit leaf table `company_dns.sic_codes` (3571, 3572, 3575, 3577). Naive inner joins silently dropped IBM's $62,753,000,000 FY2025 revenue and $730K Q3 ARR contraction.
